thesis: A calculator is a tool people trust with numbers; the interesting part is that it feels like a physical object and never lies, even on 0.1+0.2, divide by zero, or repeated equals.
job: open it and see a display at 0 and a keypad
enter digits and a decimal point by click, tap or keyboard
choose an operator (+ - x /) and see which one is pending
enter the second number, chain further operations
press equals and read the result
press equals again to repeat the last operation
correct mistakes: backspace, clear entry, all clear
read what was computed (running expression or history)
hit edge cases: divide by zero, long numbers, float noise, and recover

principles: errors are recoverable in one press
steps: map input events to a small state machine
tricks: equals repeats last op and operand
typing a digit after result starts fresh
percent relative to left operand for + and -
shrink font to fit long numbers
subtle key depth with bottom shadow
tests: can you tell digit from operator at a glance
no motion longer than 200 ms on press

principles: state object {current, previous, op, overwrite, lastOp, lastOperand, expr}
tricks: round to 12 significant digits with parseFloat(x.toPrecision(12))
keydown mapping incl. Enter, Escape, Backspace, / prevent default

kinds.name: pocket calculator

kinds.name: calculator with tape

kinds.name: expression-line calculator

descriptions: keys equal squares with 10-14 px gap

2: three tone keys: digits, utility, operators

descriptions: utility keys lighter grey than digits; operators accent; equals strongest accent

behaviors: operator pressed with pending op computes first (left to right)
equals with no op does nothing

descriptions: use real glyphs not x and /; label C when entry exists, AC otherwise

anti_keywords.instead: clear 'Cannot divide by zero' message, any key recovers
three-tier key colours with strong equals

checks: Does pressing = twice repeat the operation?
Does 5/0 show a message and recover on next key?
Does the keyboard drive everything including Backspace and Escape?
Is the pending operator visibly highlighted?
Does a 12-digit number fit the display on phone width?
